My, the room is spinning."

Vomiting denied: "Have you been physically sick?" Patient: "No". Fever denied: "Do you have a temperature at all?" Patient: "I don't think so" (implies no recorded fever). Prior brief episode: "I had a a similar sort of thing about a month ago" and when asked duration: "Probably only about five, ten minutes."
"I've had premature ovarian failure" clearly documents this past medical history.
Patient states: "and I've taken HRT," indicating hormone replacement therapy use.

Continuous vertigo, tinnitus, no hearing loss or neuro deficits are described as above, and doctor’s assessment: "the most common... diagnosis... is something called labyrinthitis" and explanation about middle ear inflammation, supporting a likely peripheral cause.
Prior brief episode is documented: "I had a a similar sort of thing about a month ago" and "Probably only about five, ten minutes."
No infectious prodrome: "Did you have any kind of viral illness in the recent past..." Patient: "No" and "No cold, cough, nothing" and "I've been pretty healthy."

The doctor sends a prescription and describes it as for middle ear stability: "we'll start you on certain medications" and "it's called , yeah? It's one tablet three times a day. So I'll give you about ten days worth." However, the specific class 'vestibular suppressant/antiemetic' is not explicitly stated; this is an inferred drug type, so it adds information beyond the transcript.

Doctor plans in-person evaluation: "I would still like you to be seen by one of our doctors to take a look inside your ears" and "we'd like to do your blood pressure, just examine your, you know, you know, how your walking and everything is," which implies gait and basic neuro assessment.

Safety net: "if you double up any weakness of your legs or arms or, or, you know, a sudden headache. Any of those symptoms, or you start being violently sick with it, then you know, you would need to take your to A and E." This covers new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, intractable vomiting/worsening symptoms.
Doctor instructs: "Just make sure you call support to book that appointment, OK?" indicating patient should book via support.

Regarding food with medication: Patient asks, "do you need to take those tablets with food?" Doctor: "It doesn't really matter, you can take it... might as well just take the tablets." This supports taking with or without food as tolerated.
